newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes flat at 251.00/80 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes flat at 251.00/80 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed around 251.00/80 per dollar, little changed from 251.50-252 in the morning after thin trade on the interbank forex market, dealers said.
"Trade was stuck within a 251-252 (levs per dollar) range throughout the day with very low volumes changing hands," a commercial bank dealer said.
The central bank was not seen supporting the lev through dollar sales like it did in the past several days, dealers said.

Dealers attributed the lev dip from 250-251.50 at the close on Thursday to local media reports the International Monetary Fund (IMF) might suspend funding to Bulgaria unless it sets up a currency board to restore confidence in the battered lev.
However, other traders said the lev fall might be considered normal under the current large spread between interest rates on lev- and dollar-denominated deposits.
The central bank's main interest rate is now set at 15 percent monthly or 180 percent annually.
An IMF mission currently in Sofia is discussing with local officials the introduction of a currency board system as a way to restore confidence in the lev, halt inflation and boost economic growth.

Currency boards, pegging the national currency to a major currency and matching the amount of local currency in circulation with the country's forex reserves, have been used in Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Argentina. @

A second $115 million tranche of IMF funding has been twice postponed since September because of the Socialist government's failure to meet reform targets under a funding deal signed in July. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 84561
